title: Antidepressant use during pregnancy and the risk of major congenital malformations in a cohort of depressed pregnant women: an updated analysis of the Quebec Pregnancy Cohort
authors: Bérard A, Zhao JP, Sheehy O
population: Pregnancies in the Quebec Pregnancy Cohort, 1998 to 2009, with a diagnosis of depression or anxiety or antidepressant exposure in the 12 months before pregnancy, ending in a live-born singleton; 3640 exposed to antidepressants in the first trimester, 365 to sertraline
funder: This study was supported by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research (grant number 132750). AB is the recipient of a research chair from the Fonds de la recherche du Québec—Santé.
authorConflicts: AB is a consultant for plaintiffs in litigations involving antidepressants and birth defects.
result: First-trimester sertraline and major congenital malformations: adjusted OR 1.09 (95% CI 0.80 to 1.50); nervous system 1.72 (0.69 to 4.26). Citalopram: major malformations 1.36 (1.08 to 1.73), craniosynostosis 3.95 (2.08 to 7.52); paroxetine: cardiac defects 1.45 (1.12 to 1.88).
